result:
Race condition: result depends on unpredictable timing of concurrent processes touching shared state. Two writers interleave → lost, garbled, or overwritten lines.

For log appends, open with `>>` and emit each record as one write:

```sh
printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >> "$LOG"
```

`>>` opens with `O_APPEND` → kernel seeks to end and writes atomically, so writers can't overwrite each other. Unsafe: `>` (truncates), read-modify-write (`cat`/edit/write back), or building one record from several `echo`s, since other writers can land between them.

Multi-line records, or check-then-write logic, need a lock:

```sh
(
  flock 9
  echo "begin $job"
  run_job
  echo "end $job"
) 9>"$LOG.lock" >>"$LOG"
```

`flock` (util-linux) blocks until the lock is free and releases it when fd 9 closes, even on crash.

Caveats: `O_APPEND` is not atomic on NFS, so use `flock` there or ship through `logger`/syslog. Very large single writes can be split, so keep records to a line. All writers must use the same lock file, because `flock` is advisory.
